data.name: Fathan
data.gender_notes: Fathan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Fathan is derived from the Arabic root 'fatha' which means 'to open'. In Islamic context, it is mentioned in the Hadith that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) used this name for his horse. The name is also said to symbolize the spiritual opening of one's eyes to the truth and guidance of Allah. The name Fathan carries the meaning “Opener, Opener of the eyes” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fathan usually hope their child will grow to embody opener, opener of the eyes and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: During the Battle of Siffin, the forces of Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan clashed. Both leaders rode white horses, Ali on his horse named Murad, and Muawiya on his horse named Fathan. The battle ended in a stalemate, and eventually, the matter was resolved through arbitration, not through military victory.
